design_detail: Meta-analysis of (C)BT studies and pharmacotherapy studies for generalized anxiety disorder, including a subset of studies directly comparing both
population: Patients with generalized anxiety disorder (not perinatal-specific)
sample_size_detail: 65 (C)BT and pharmacological studies included; pooled participant total not reported in abstract
rationale: PubMed type Meta-Analysis; abstract states 65 (C)BT and pharmacological studies were meta-analyzed. Whether component studies were randomized and the pooled N are not given.

design_detail: Recommendation statement on depression screening in adults (CMAJ); no abstract in file
population: Adults (general population; per title)
sample_size_detail: Not applicable (guideline)
rationale: Title 'Recommendations on screening for depression in adults' and PubMed type Practice Guideline. No abstract; coded from metadata only.

design_detail: RANZCOG best practice statement on mental health care in the perinatal period (C-Obs 48)
population: Perinatal women (Australia/New Zealand practice)
sample_size_detail: Not applicable (guideline)
rationale: Citation identifies a professional college 'Best practice statement'; citation only, no abstract or full text.

design_detail: J Reprod Infant Psychol 2012 article on patient-, provider-, and system-level barriers and facilitators to addressing perinatal depression; not indexed in PubMed, design not determinable from citation
severity_measure: Design and analysis not determinable from citation alone
population: Perinatal depression care (patients, providers, and systems, per title)
sample_size_detail: Not available (citation only)
rationale: Coded from ACOG citation only (corrected file; earlier file held a wrong abstract, disregarded). The barriers/facilitators title fits a qualitative study or a review, but the design cannot be confirmed, so coded Other (indeterminate).

design_detail: Online ACOG webinar/training course (UMass Chan Medical School) on addressing perinatal mental health conditions in obstetric settings
population: Obstetric clinicians (training resource on perinatal mental health)
sample_size_detail: Not applicable (resource)
rationale: Citation is to a pathlms.com ACOG webinar course page, i.e., a training program, not a study.

design_detail: Cross-sectional survey of a sample of 1000 ACOG Fellows on prenatal depression screening and antidepressant prescribing; descriptive with bivariate association tests
comparison_group: None (descriptive; association of SSRI prescribing with evidence interpretation)
population: US obstetrician-gynecologists (ACOG Fellows) providing prenatal care
sample_size_detail: 1000 Fellows sampled; 379 responded (37.9%); 288 provided care to pregnant patients and answered the depression/antidepressant questions
rationale: Clinician survey of practices and opinions; no patient-level comparative effect estimate. Participants are clinicians, not perinatal patients.

design_detail: Pre/post-implementation cohort (planned secondary analysis of a prospective cohort), single US academic center EHR; propensity-score covariate adjustment with race-by-epoch interaction terms; no concurrent control
severity_measure: Propensity score included maternal age, insurance, parity, tobacco, substance use history, chronic medical condition, and presence of mental health history only; no severity measure (PHQ-9 used only to define positive screen)
comparison_group: Pre-implementation epoch (2015–2016); White individuals as race referent
population: Black and White pregnant/postpartum people receiving prenatal care at Northwestern Medicine collaborative-care-affiliated practices, Chicago, deliveries 2015–2016 vs 2017–2019
sample_size_detail: Pre-implementation 2286 (262 Black, 2024 White); post-implementation 2424 (313 Black, 2111 White); treatment-recommendation analyses restricted to positive screens (small subgroups)
rationale: Two delivery-date epochs before/after collaborative care model implementation without a concurrent control, so not quasi-experimental per protocol. Methods list propensity-score covariates; only presence of mental health history, no severity proxy.

design_detail: Descriptive program evaluation of MCPAP for Moms (statewide perinatal psychiatry access program): enrollment, trainings, consultations, cost
population: Massachusetts obstetric practices and pregnant/postpartum women served by MCPAP for Moms, first 18 months
sample_size_detail: 87 Ob/Gyn practices enrolled, 100 trainings, 1123 women served; no comparison group
rationale: Reports program development, utilization volume, and per-capita cost without a comparative effect estimate.

design_detail: Cross-sectional analysis of nationally representative survey data, 2005–2009; chi-square tests and adjusted prevalence ratios of diagnosis/treatment by pregnancy status among women with past-year MDE
severity_measure: Adjusted prevalence ratios reported but covariates not listed in abstract; sample restricted to women meeting past-year MDE criteria (diagnosis only)
comparison_group: Nonpregnant women aged 18–44 with past-year MDE
population: US women aged 18–44 meeting criteria for past-year major depressive episode, 2005–2009
sample_size_detail: 375 pregnant and 8657 nonpregnant women with past-year MDE
rationale: Non-randomized comparison by pregnancy status with adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR); adjustment set unavailable in abstract, so severity Unclear and coded 4 by default.

design_detail: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of double-blind RCTs of 21 antidepressants vs placebo or head-to-head for acute MDD (PROSPERO registered)
population: Adults with major depressive disorder (not perinatal-specific)
sample_size_detail: 522 double-blind parallel RCTs comprising 116477 patients (1979–2016)
rationale: Explicit SR/NMA restricted to double-blind RCTs; quasi-randomised trials excluded. Counts confirmed in Results.

design_detail: Systematic review, random-effects meta-analysis, and network meta-analysis of cohort and case-control studies on prenatal SSRI/SNRI exposure and PPHN
population: Offspring of women exposed vs unexposed to SSRIs/SNRIs during pregnancy
sample_size_detail: Abstract reports only exposed: 156978 women/offspring exposed to SSRIs/SNRIs (452 PPHN cases); total pooled including unexposed not reported
rationale: Included retrospective cohort and case-control studies only. Total pooled N not given (only exposed count), so sample_size_n left null.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis (comparative effectiveness) of antidepressant treatment for depression in pregnancy and postpartum
comparison_group: Placebo, no treatment, other antidepressants, or nondrug treatments
population: Pregnant and postpartum women with depression (plus indirect evidence from women taking antidepressants for any reason)
sample_size_detail: 6 RCTs and 15 observational studies; pooled participant total not reported in abstract
rationale: Abstract states 'Six randomized controlled trials and 15 observational studies provided evidence'.

design_detail: Single-center, 6-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of flexibly dosed sertraline after 1-week single-blind placebo lead-in
population: Women aged 18–45 with major depression onset within 3 months of delivery, Connecticut, recruited 1994–2004
sample_size_detail: 38 entered placebo lead-in, 2 removed; 36 randomized (17 sertraline, 19 placebo) = ITT; 33 evaluable; 29 completed week 7; strict DSM-IV onset subset 27 (ITT)
rationale: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial; abstract's n=38 counts lead-in entrants, while Results give 36 randomized.

design_detail: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of placebo- and active-controlled randomised trials of pharmacological treatments for GAD (PROSPERO registered)
population: Adult outpatients with generalised anxiety disorder (not perinatal-specific)
sample_size_detail: 89 trials; 25441 patients randomly assigned to 22 active drugs or placebo
rationale: Abstract: SR/NMA 'performed on randomised trials'; 89 trials with 25441 randomized patients.

design_detail: Clinical review (Obstet Gynecol Clin North Am) of screening, risks, pharmacotherapy, dosing, and nondrug treatment of peripartum bipolar disorder; no systematic search methods
population: Pregnant and postpartum women with bipolar disorder
sample_size_detail: Not applicable (narrative review)
rationale: PubMed type Review; full text is topical clinical overview with no search strategy, selection criteria, or pooled analysis.

design_detail: Danish registry linkage (Medical Birth Register and Psychiatric Central Register, 1973–1993); relative risk of psychosis admission within 91 days after delivery vs non-puerperal women
severity_measure: RRs reported but abstract never states whether adjusted (Amendment 1b); first admissions and readmissions reported separately
comparison_group: Non-puerperal women in the general Danish female population
population: Danish women 1973–1993 (postpartum vs non-puerperal)
sample_size_detail: 1253 psychosis admissions within 91 days after delivery; denominators (deliveries, person-time, comparison admissions) not given in abstract
rationale: Registry rate comparison of postpartum vs non-puerperal admission rates (RR); abstract does not say whether RRs are adjusted, so coded unadjusted/Unclear/Low per Amendment 1(b). Exposure is childbirth, not treatment.

design_detail: Two-part study: systematic review of 8 cohort studies to identify candidate malformations, then population-based case-malformed-control study in EUROCAT Antiepileptic Study Database (19 European registries, 1995–2005) testing them; logistic regression adjusted for maternal age, birth year, registry
severity_measure: Adjusted only for maternal age, year of birth, and reporting registry; no epilepsy type or seizure measures (authors note no other confounder data available)
comparison_group: No AED exposure; valproic acid monotherapy; other AED monotherapy (two malformed control groups: non-chromosomal and chromosomal)
population: Registered congenital anomaly cases (live births, fetal deaths ≥20 weeks, terminations) in 19 European registries, 1995–2005
sample_size_detail: Case-control: 11790 cases (5 malformation subgroups), 69883 non-chromosomal controls, 11763 chromosomal controls; 131 carbamazepine-monotherapy-exposed registrations. SR component: 8 cohort studies, 2680 CBZ-exposed pregnancies (not counted here)
rationale: Main confirmatory estimates (e.g., spina bifida aOR 2.6) come from the adjusted case-control analysis, which precedes SR in the decision order; SR component only generated hypotheses. Adjustment set lacks any severity measure.

design_detail: Multicenter prospective observational PK study with frequent preconception and early-pregnancy sampling; population mixed-effects modeling of lamotrigine clearance vs gestational week and estradiol
comparison_group: None (within-woman change from preconception; low vs high clearance-change groups)
population: Women with epilepsy on lamotrigine without interacting medications, before and during early pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 25 pregnancies in 22 participants
rationale: Drug-clearance modeling study with no clinical outcome comparison.

design_detail: Prospective PK study: lamotrigine concentrations preconception and monthly through pregnancy and after childbirth; clearance compared across trimesters
population: Women on lamotrigine monotherapy during pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 14 women on LTG monotherapy
rationale: Measures lamotrigine clearance changes across pregnancy; purely pharmacokinetic.

design_detail: Longitudinal PK analysis of steady-state lamotrigine levels, dose, and weight preconception, each trimester, and postpartum; ANOVA and paired t-tests
population: Pregnant women taking lamotrigine (with or without concomitant AEDs)
sample_size_detail: 12 pregnancies with complete steady-state data before, during, and after pregnancy
rationale: Apparent clearance compared across pregnancy periods; dose-requirement PK study.

design_detail: Prospective observational study of placental passage (umbilical cord-to-maternal plasma ratio) of atypical antipsychotics and haloperidol at delivery, with descriptive obstetrical outcomes
population: Pregnant women with laboratory-confirmed antipsychotic use proximate to delivery
sample_size_detail: 54 women analyzed; complete maternal-cord sample pairs for 50
rationale: Primary aim is quantifying placental passage; obstetric outcomes are descriptive with no adjusted comparison.

design_detail: 8-week double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of quetiapine 600 or 300 mg/day monotherapy
population: Outpatients with bipolar I or II disorder in a major depressive episode (not perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 542 randomized (360 bipolar I, 182 bipolar II); analyzed N not given in abstract
rationale: Participants 'randomly assigned' to quetiapine doses or placebo; PubMed type Randomized Controlled Trial.

design_detail: 8-week multicenter double-blind placebo-controlled RCT (BOLDER II) of quetiapine 300 or 600 mg/day monotherapy
population: Patients with bipolar I or II disorder in a depressive episode (not perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 509 randomized; 59% completed; primary analysis ANCOVA with LOCF
rationale: Abstract: 'Of 509 patients randomized'; double-blind placebo-controlled trial.

design_detail: 8-week multicenter double-blind placebo-controlled RCT (EMBOLDEN I) of quetiapine 300/600 mg/day and lithium monotherapy
population: Adults with bipolar I or II disorder in an acute major depressive episode, 2005–2007 (not perinatal)
sample_size_detail: Randomized: quetiapine 300 mg n=265, quetiapine 600 mg n=268, lithium n=136, placebo n=133
rationale: 802 patients 'randomly allocated' to four arms; registered trial NCT00206141.

design_detail: Systematic review of systematic reviews (overview) on lurasidone for bipolar depression; AMSTAR/R-AMSTAR quality appraisal; narrative synthesis, no meta-analysis
comparison_group: NA (underlying trials: lurasidone vs placebo/adjunctive comparisons)
population: Patients with bipolar disorder treated with lurasidone (not perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 12 included systematic reviews (covering a handful of RCTs); no pooled participant count
rationale: Umbrella review with protocol, multi-database search, dual screening; included units are systematic reviews (SRs of RCTs or observational studies eligible), so component designs not stated.

design_detail: Single-patient case report with serial lurasidone serum concentrations from second trimester to 3 months postpartum, alongside bipolar symptom monitoring
population: One primiparous woman with bipolar disorder treated with lurasidone in pregnancy and postpartum
sample_size_detail: Single case
rationale: PubMed type Case Reports, but the primary content is serial drug concentrations across pregnancy; PK precedes case report in the decision order.

design_detail: Prospective cohort of infants of women with epilepsy receiving valproic acid (mono- or polytherapy) compared with matched-pair controls and controls from a larger AED study; also VPA serum concentrations
severity_measure: Matched-pair controls but matching variables not given in abstract; no seizure type/frequency measure mentioned
comparison_group: 26 matched-pair controls and 116 controls from a larger antiepileptic drug study
population: Infants of women with epilepsy receiving valproic acid during pregnancy
sample_size_detail: 14 VPA-monotherapy and 12 VPA-combination-exposed infants; 26 matched-pair controls; 116 additional controls
rationale: Comparative prospective cohort with matched controls (matching counts as adjustment), but matching factors are unknown from abstract, so adjustment and severity cannot be verified.

design_detail: Lancet research letter (PubMed: Comparative Study; Letter) on in-utero valproate exposure and neural tube defects; no abstract, design details unavailable
severity_measure: No abstract; cannot determine whether any adjustment was made
population: Pregnancies/offspring exposed to valproate in utero
sample_size_detail: Not available in file
rationale: Only title and publication types (Comparative Study; Letter) available; a crude comparative letter is the best guess but design is not verifiable.

design_detail: Prospective multinational cohort (Japan, Italy, Canada) of offspring of mothers with epilepsy; malformation incidence by AED exposure, regimen, dose and serum level; background risk factors examined
severity_measure: Abstract reports crude incidences; background factors were examined but method and covariates (e.g., seizure type/frequency) not stated
comparison_group: Offspring without AED exposure; comparisons across AEDs and polytherapy
population: Offspring of women with epilepsy in Japan, Italy, and Canada
sample_size_detail: 983 offspring prospectively analyzed; exposed/unexposed split not given in abstract
rationale: Results are crude incidence comparisons; 'background factors studied' may imply a multivariable analysis, so adjustment status uncertain. Sibling malformation history is a risk factor, not a within-family design.

design_detail: Letter-format case report (PubMed: Case Reports; Letter) on valproic acid teratogenicity; no abstract
population: Infant(s) exposed to valproic acid in utero
sample_size_detail: Number of cases not available in file
rationale: Design inferred from PubMed publication types (Case Reports; Letter) and title; no abstract to confirm case count.

design_detail: Case series describing dysmorphic phenotype in infants exposed to valproate in pregnancy
population: Infants exposed to sodium valproate/valproic acid in utero
sample_size_detail: 4 exposed infants (3 surviving)
rationale: 'Four infants who were exposed... are described'; no comparison group.

design_detail: Single case report of a male child with fetal valproate syndrome and autism
population: One male child with prenatal valproate exposure
sample_size_detail: Single patient
rationale: 'We report on a patient'; PubMed type Case Reports.

design_detail: Cohort follow-up at age 5.5 years comparing children of mothers with epilepsy vs control children; within-group risk-factor analysis (maternal seizure type, seizures in pregnancy, AED exposure, paternal education)
severity_measure: Study vs control comparison appears crude; within-group analysis examined maternal partial seizures and seizures during pregnancy alongside AED exposure, but whether this was multivariable is not stated
population: Children of mothers with epilepsy (89% AED-exposed in utero) and control children, all of normal general intelligence
sample_size_detail: 104 children of epileptic mothers, 105 control children
rationale: Comparative cohort with apparently crude group comparisons; within-group risk-factor analysis included epilepsy-severity-type factors but the analytic method is not described in the abstract.

design_detail: Lancet 1970 article on neonatal coagulation defect after maternal anticonvulsant treatment; no abstract, design cannot be determined
population: Neonates of mothers treated with anticonvulsants during pregnancy
sample_size_detail: Not available in file
rationale: File has only title and PubMed type 'Journal Article'; could be a case series, physiologic study, or comparative study, so coded Other (indeterminate).

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis (reported per MOOSE) of antipsychotic clinical trials reporting weight/BMI change, stratified by drug and exposure duration; PubMed/Embase 1999–2011
comparison_group: Other antipsychotics or placebo; AP-naive subgroup
population: Adults (≥18) treated with antipsychotics in clinical trials, any diagnosis (not perinatal)
sample_size_detail: 307 included papers (257 reported weight change; 603 meta-analysis records); total pooled participants not reported
rationale: Inclusion criteria list RCTs/controlled clinical trials, and Discussion states 'only RCTs were included'. No pooled participant total reported.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis of metabolic syndrome prevalence and relative risk across schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and MDD, with moderator analyses
comparison_group: Between-diagnosis comparisons; matched general population controls; antipsychotic-naive participants
population: People with schizophrenia/related psychoses, bipolar disorder, or major depressive disorder (not perinatal)
sample_size_detail: Pooled MetS prevalence: N=198 (studies/datasets), n=52678 participants with severe mental illness
rationale: Abstract describes SR/MA; '198' is the N reported for the pooled prevalence analysis and may count datasets rather than papers. Component designs not stated.

design_detail: Two population-based retrospective cohorts (UK THIN and Hong Kong CDARS) of women with pre-pregnancy antipsychotic use, continuers vs discontinuers; propensity-score fine-stratification weighting; plus an updated meta-analysis (secondary)
severity_measure: PS fine-stratification weighting used, but covariates not listed in abstract; restriction to prior antipsychotic users is not itself a severity measure
comparison_group: Women prescribed antipsychotics before pregnancy who stopped during pregnancy (discontinuers)
population: Nondiabetic women with antipsychotic prescriptions before their first pregnancy, UK (THIN) and Hong Kong (CDARS)
sample_size_detail: 2351 in THIN and 763 in CDARS (first pregnancies); continuer/discontinuer split not in abstract; meta-analysis N not reported
rationale: Primary aim and estimates come from PS-weighted cohort analyses, so coded observational rather than meta-analysis; adjustment set unavailable in abstract.

design_detail: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies of GDM risk in women with preconception mental disorders; risk-of-bias checklist, dual review
comparison_group: Women without the preconception mental disorder
population: Pregnant women with preconception mood, anxiety, psychotic, or eating disorders
sample_size_detail: 22 observational studies (mostly retrospective cohorts); pooled participant total not reported
rationale: Abstract: '22 observational studies met inclusion criteria'; pooled ORs by disorder.

design_detail: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of case-control, cohort, and interventional studies of lithium safety and efficacy in pregnancy and postpartum; NOS and Cochrane risk-of-bias tools
comparison_group: Lithium-unexposed pregnancies/women (incl. bipolar disorder without lithium)
population: Pregnant and postpartum women (focus on bipolar disorder) and their offspring
sample_size_detail: 29 studies (13 in quantitative analysis); outcome-specific N: any congenital anomaly 23300 (k=11), cardiac anomalies 1348475 (k=12), spontaneous abortion 1289 (k=3), postpartum relapse 48 (k=2); no overall total
rationale: SR/MA including observational and interventional designs; only outcome-specific pooled Ns given, so overall N left null.

design_detail: Prospective longitudinal PK study: serial 12–24 h blood sampling and urine collection each trimester and postpartum, 1-compartment model of lithium elimination clearance, with mood symptom ratings
population: Pregnant women with bipolar I disorder treated with lithium, Northwestern University (Chicago)
sample_size_detail: 4 enrolled, 1 withdrew; 3 completed and analyzed; 182 serum samples
rationale: Characterizes lithium clearance and serum concentrations across pregnancy with no comparative clinical outcome analysis.

design_detail: Systematic review (PubMed 1995–2015) of reports on mood stabilizer exposure via breast milk: relative infant dose, milk-to-plasma ratio, infant serum levels, adverse events; no meta-analysis
population: Breastfed infants of lactating women taking mood stabilizers
sample_size_detail: 26 reports: lamotrigine 122 cases (12 reports), lithium 26 (5), carbamazepine 64 (5), valproate 9 (3), oxcarbazepine 2 (2); no overall total reported (one report covered two drugs)
rationale: Included case reports, case series, and prospective/cross-sectional studies; drug-specific case counts given but no total.

design_detail: Retrospective cohort, Kaiser Permanente Washington EHR linked to Washington birth records, 2001–2014; prior antidepressant users, continuers vs discontinuers; IPTW with GEE (Poisson for RR)
severity_measure: IPTW included prior-year psychiatry visits, psychotherapy visits, inpatient psychiatric hospitalization, psychotropic fills (antipsychotic, benzodiazepine, mood stabilizer), and mental health diagnoses; PHQ-9 described but not modeled
comparison_group: Women with antidepressant fills in 6 months before pregnancy who did not fill during pregnancy (discontinuers)
population: Women aged 15–45 without pre-existing diabetes with an antidepressant fill ≤6 months before pregnancy; singleton live births, KPWA 2001–2014
sample_size_detail: 1634 continuers, 1211 discontinuers; blood glucose subanalysis 1101 births (613/488); about 4% missing covariates excluded from regression
rationale: Methods and Table 1 show IPTW covariates included psychiatric hospitalization, psychiatry visits, and psychotropic fills, all severity proxies; GEE handles repeat births and is not a sibling contrast.
